title: Grunewald classes, Professor Hogan and being self-taught
summary: Cotton says Grunewald gave books but little real playing, then he took private lessons with Professor Hogan; he was largely self-taught.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: you were coming up, or when you... Well, no. When I went to, when I went to

Grunewald, it was, it was, man, guys was hanging around with pencils in their bag pocket, and all they wanted to do was sign in the paper, just to get the money. But I went to line. I went and got as much as I could out of the year and six months I think it was that I had over there. About eighteen months that I had over there. I got as much as I could out of that. But the actual play and the actual do things over there, it never happened.
What if the teachers didn't sit down with you? They gave you books. They gave you, and

they gave you... I have a lot of stuff that I... from Grunewald that I had. You know, all kind of theory, harmony, and I don't know, all kind of things like that, you know. And you could always refer back to these type of things, but I never did use any of that stuff. And then while I was gone, I went to Professor Hogan. After I left Grunewald School, I went for private lessons over there, and he was teaching me a few things about handling and a little few classical things, you know. And then later on when I got to the Rogers I showed him some of the things and he got me playing, I'm playing a variety of things.
